findings.title: missing_backup_codes message points to a settings option that does not exist
findings.body: The message says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Nothing in this PR adds a way to generate or regenerate backup codes from settings. Codes are only created during the initial 2FA setup, and disabling 2FA is the only way back to setup. Users who enabled 2FA before this change have no codes, and the "Lost access" path shows this message with no working next step. The text should not promise a settings action that is not implemented.

findings.title: Backup code can be redeemed more than once under concurrent logins
findings.body: The backup code is read from the DB, checked with indexOf, nulled in memory, and written back in a separate prisma.user.update with no transaction, row lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent login attempts with the same valid code (for example a double-submit or a parallel request) both read the old list, both pass the check, and both write back. A single-use code is therefore accepted twice. The consume step should be an atomic conditional update or run inside a transaction that re-checks the stored value.

findings.title: Backup codes can be dismissed without being saved, leaving the user locked out
findings.body: The dialog is opened with onOpenChange, so Escape or clicking the overlay closes it during the DisplayBackupCodes step without going through the Close button. The codes are only shown once, and nothing forces the user to copy or download them or confirm they have been saved. Since 2FA is already enabled at this point and there is no regeneration path, a user who loses their authenticator and never saved the codes is locked out of the account. The backup-codes step should block dismissal or ask for confirmation.

findings.title: type="password" prop overrides PasswordField's show/hide toggle
findings.body: PasswordField sets type from its visibility state and then spreads {...props}. Passing type="password" here overrides that value, so the visibility toggle on this password field never reveals the text. This is a regression from the TextField it replaced, which had no toggle. Remove the explicit type prop.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order
findings.body: The new tabIndex={-1} takes the show/hide password button out of keyboard navigation for every PasswordField in the app. Keyboard and screen-reader users can no longer reach the toggle. The change is not related to backup codes and is an accessibility regression for all password inputs.

findings.title: Backup code login, the main new login feature, has no test
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose includes logging in with a backup code via "Lost access", and the test-plan step asks for this. The only e2e changes cover setup and the download/copy/close buttons. Nothing tests that a backup code logs in, that it is single-use after login, that a wrong code shows the error, or that disabling 2FA with a backup code works. The TODO acknowledges this, but the feature ships untested, and the consumption logic in next-auth-options.ts has no unit test.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes an unhandled exception
findings.body: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...) assumes a string. A client sending a number or object for backupCode (it is truthy, so the branch is taken) throws a TypeError outside any try/catch, producing a 500 rather than a 400 error response. The same pattern is in next-auth-options.ts line 144. Validate the type before calling string methods.

findings.title: Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed
findings.body: Backup codes are stored as a symmetric-encrypted JSON array, so anyone with the encryption key (or a DB read plus key access) can recover all unused codes in plaintext. Single-use credentials are normally stored as salted hashes, which lets the server verify them without retaining the secrets. Because the codes are only needed for comparison, hashing them is the expected approach.
